To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PI3Kβ is uniquely required for the generation of synergistic PIP 3 responses to coincident stimulation of GPCRs (e.g., complement receptor 3) and receptor tyroside kinases (e.g., macrophage colony stimulating factor receptor) and is required for the generation and maintenance of neutrophil adhesion in response to FcγR activation and β2 integrin activation.
p110β is the only PI3K catalyytic isoform that mediates synergistic PIPK production upon coincident activation of macrophages via M-CSF and GPCRs.

p110β is uniquely required for synergistic PI3K signaling from GPCRs that are coincident with RTKs, and this is essential for macrophage responses to M-CSF and C5a and neutrophil functions in immune complex clearance and adhesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the p110β isoform in signaling by the PI3K family of enzymes.
the regulation and function of the PI3K family of enzymes in immune cells.
how cells integrate signals from multiple receptors and how this process is regulated in disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PI3Kβ-Gβγ complex is required for synergistic signaling from RTK and GPCRs in myeloid immune cells.

p110β is uniquely required for the generation of PIP3 in macrophages and for the generation of reactive oxygen species and β2 integrin-mediated adhesion in neutrophils upon simultaneous stimulation by RTKs and GPCRs, and that this function depends on the ability of p110β to interact with Gβγ.
the PI3Kβ isoform is uniquely able to mediate synergistic signaling in myeloid immune cells upon simultaneous stimulation of GPCR and RTKs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p110β is a unique PI3K isoformer, in that its ability to transduce signals from both RTKs and GPCRs can be exploited to synergistically enhance PIP3 formation.
p110β mediates synergism in the signaling of two receptors that have been shown to synergize in vivo.
PI3Kβ is uniquely required to mediate synergistic signaling from GPCRs with receptor tyrosine tyrosine kinse (RTKs).
The main takeaway from our work is that
PI3Kβ is uniquely required to transduce signals from GPCRS and receptor tyrosin kinases in immune cell signaling.
p110β is uniquely required for GPCR and RTK synergy in macrophages and for neutrophils’ responses to Fcγ receptor and integrin engagement, respectively.
p110β has a unique role in mediating the synergistic signaling downstream of coincident stimulation of an RTK and a GPCR.
